subject.title: feat(plugin-sdk): generic outbound delivery-report seam; WhatsApp native auto-reply reports provider-accepted sends

question: Should OpenClaw accept this new public plugin SDK delivery-report subpath as the supported contract for self-delivered channel sends?
rationale: The code path is plausible, but publishing a new SDK seam fixes the compatibility contract for third-party plugins and automation should not choose that API shape without maintainer intent.

options.title: Accept Seam After Proof
options.body: Require redacted WhatsApp/runtime proof and maintainer acceptance of the subpath name, payload fields, and idempotency semantics before merge.

options.title: Narrow Or Rename API
options.body: Keep the branch open but ask for a smaller or differently named public contract if maintainers want a stricter SDK boundary.

options.title: Pause API Design
options.body: Leave the linked issue as the design point if maintainers are not ready to publish a self-delivery reporting contract.

recommendation.title: Accept Seam After Proof
recommendation.body: Require redacted WhatsApp/runtime proof and maintainer acceptance of the subpath name, payload fields, and idempotency semantics before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans plugin SDK, channel delivery, and hook lifecycle contracts, and steipete is the strongest routing candidate from adjacent sent-hook refinement history.
